prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

MPT arithmetic under MPTokensV2 uses Number, and a 19-digit MPT amount
doesn't fit the small 16-digit mantissa that transactions use unless
SingleAssetVault or LendingProtocol is enabled. Add MPTokensV2 to the
amendments that enable the large mantissa, so MPT math never runs at
the small scale regardless of activation order.

The IOU AMM tests keep the small mantissa, as they do for
SingleAssetVault and LendingProtocol. The MPT AMM tests now run with
the large mantissa, and their expected values are updated.

## API Impact

- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [ ] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)
- [ ] Peer protocol change (must be backward compatible or bump the peer protocol version)

## Test Plan

- Test changes:
  - `testAMM()` and the IOU AMM suites (AMM, AMMExtended, AMMClawback) strip MPTokensV2 for pools without an MPT asset, so they keep the small mantissa, as they already do for SingleAssetVault and LendingProtocol.
  - EscrowToken and AMMClawbackMPT treat MPTokensV2 as enabling the large mantissa.
  - AMMMPT and AMMExtendedMPT expected values are updated to the large-mantissa results. Most are more precise (LP tokens, withdraw remainders, a full single-sided deposit that the small mantissa rounded down by one unit). A few move by one unit because of the AMM's rounding in the pool's favor. One "calculated tokens are 0" withdraw uses 1e-16 USD, since the previous 1e-11 now yields valid nonzero tokens.
  - No IOU or XRP test expectations change.
- Verified with MPTokensV2 on and SingleAssetVault/LendingProtocol off. Before this change, `divide(maxMPT, 1)` threw a Number overflow and an MPT AMM clawback returned `tecINTERNAL`. With the large mantissa, both behave correctly.

reviews.body: This MR extends the large-Number-mantissa gating (Rules.cpp) to include featureMPTokensV2, and updates the various AMM/Escrow test suites and their expected values accordingly. The core Rules.cpp change is correct and consistent with the existing pattern (both enableLargeNumbers and useRulesGuards updated together). Most test-value updates look like mechanical adjustments to reflect increased precision and are consistent with the PR description. One real issue found: redefining `all` in AMMClawback_test.cpp to already exclude featureMPTokensV2 makes the very next `testInvalidRequest(all - featureMPTokensV2)` call identical to `testInvalidRequest(all)`, silently dropping coverage of the 'MPTokensV2 enabled' scenario for invalid-request tests.

reviews.body: This is a well-scoped, mechanical change that adds featureMPTokensV2 to the amendment set that enables the large Number mantissa (Rules.cpp), updates documentation comments to match (Number.h), and adjusts test suites to track the new behavior. The test updates are internally consistent with the MR description: AMMTest.cpp now only keeps featureMPTokensV2 enabled for pools that actually contain an MPT asset (preserving small-mantissa IOU/XRP-only test coverage), and the various MPT-specific test suites (AMMMPT_test.cpp, AMMExtendedMPT_test.cpp, AMMClawbackMPT_test.cpp, EscrowToken_test.cpp) update their large-mantissa detection and expected numeric values accordingly, with explanatory comments added where values shifted by rounding. The Rules.cpp wiring (enableLargeNumbers / useRulesGuards) correctly ORs in featureMPTokensV2 alongside the existing SingleAssetVault/LendingProtocol checks, matching the existing pattern. I did not find any clear correctness, security, or consistency issues introduced by this diff — the logic changes are narrowly scoped, each behavioral change is tied to an explanation in the MR description, and no new raw conditions were left unmigrated to the new largeMantissa helper in the hunks shown.

reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body: This rejects valid bids, because the future input transfer rate is context-dependent. For example, with zero outstanding supply, a holder can bid for `MaximumAmount` of a fee-bearing MPT and the issuer can take that bid by issuing exactly `MaximumAmount`; `BookOfferCrossingStep::getOfrInRate` uses parity when the preceding MPT endpoint issues, so no gross-up or overflow occurs. This unconditional asset-rate check nevertheless returns `tecKILLED`. Avoid deciding restability from the raw transfer rate here; the crossing path needs to apply the effective rate (and partial limits) for the actual taker.

reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body: Enabling the large scale here changes `Number` arithmetic for every transaction under MPTokensV2, including pure IOU/XRP paths. The added BookStep tests explicitly expect MPTokensV2 to change pure IOU and XRP offer outcomes, while the PR overview describes only MPT arithmetic and says IOU/XRP expectations do not change. This consensus-scope expansion should either be constrained to MPT operations or explicitly documented and reviewed as a non-MPT behavior change.

issues.title: DomainID accepted on direct XRP and pre-MPTokensV2 MPT payments imposes unnecessary restriction
issues.author: mvadari
issues.body:
**Severity**: LOW\
**Attack vector**: AV-005

The Payment preflight does not reject sfDomainID for direct XRP payments or pre-MPTokensV2 direct MPT payments. The preclaim then checks that both source and destination accounts are in the domain (lines 391-398), even though no offers are consumed and the domain restriction is meaningless for direct transfers. This imposes an unnecessary constraint: both accounts must hold valid credentials for the domain, even for simple XRP/MPT transfers. While not a security vulnerability, it's a correctness issue that could lead to unexpected tecNO\_PERMISSION failures for direct payments that should not require domain membership.

**Root cause**: The preclaim DomainID check is applied unconditionally to all Payment transactions without checking whether the payment actually uses the DEX (offers/paths). For direct transfers, the domain restriction serves no purpose.

`src/libxrpl/tx/transactors/payment/Payment.cpp:391-398`

```cpp
if (ctx.tx.isFieldPresent(sfDomainID))
{
 if (!permissioned_dex::accountInDomain(ctx.view, ctx.tx[sfAccount], ctx.tx[sfDomainID]))
 return tecNO_PERMISSION;
 if (!permissioned_dex::accountInDomain(ctx.view, ctx.tx[sfDestination], ctx.tx[sfDomainID]))
 return tecNO_PERMISSION;
}
```

**Invariant gap**: PermissionedDEX invariant passes trivially when no offers are touched.

**Suggested fix**: Either reject sfDomainID in preflight for direct XRP payments (and pre-MPTokensV2 direct MPT payments), or skip the domain check in preclaim when the payment doesn't use the DEX.

### Triage Details

**Status**: ✅ Verified

Confirmed. Payment.cpp lines 391-398 check sfDomainID unconditionally for all payment types. For direct XRP or pre-MPTokensV2 direct MPT payments, no offers are consumed and no DEX interaction occurs, so the domain restriction serves no purpose. However, this is not a security vulnerability — it imposes an unnecessary restriction (requiring domain membership for direct transfers) rather than allowing any bypass. It makes the user experience worse but doesn't enable any attack.

| Dimension | Value |
| --- | --- |
| amendment\_required | Permissioned DEX amendment |
| mainnet\_exposure | False |

**Final severity**: INFORMATIONAL

**Action**: Backlog

This is a design issue, not a security vulnerability. The DomainID field imposes an unnecessary but harmless restriction on direct payments. Users can simply omit the DomainID field for direct transfers. A fix would either reject sfDomainID in preflight for non-DEX payments, or skip the domain check in preclaim when no paths/offers are involved.

Either reject sfDomainID in preflight when the payment is a direct transfer (no paths, no SendMax for IOU, direct MPT pre-V2), or skip the domain check in preclaim when the payment won't touch the DEX.

---

### False Positives (6)

- **BUG-U004**: Pre-fixDelegateV1\_1: delegated payments miss cross-currency SendMax check for PaymentMint/PaymentBurn Before fixDelegateV1\_1, the Payment::checkPermission function does not validate that sfSendMax has the same asset as sfAmount when granting PaymentMint or PaymentBurn delegated permissions. This allows a delegate with PaymentMint or PaymentBurn to execute cross-currency payments on behalf of the delegator. The post-amendment code at lines 278-280 adds this check. This is a known issue fixed by the fixDelegateV1\_1 amendment.
- **BUG-U005**: Pre-fixMPTDeliveredAmount: metadata does not reflect actual delivered amount for MPT partial payments Before fixMPTDeliveredAmount, when an MPT partial payment delivers less than the requested amount (due to partial payment flag or transfer rate adjustment), the DeliveredAmount metadata field is not set. Downstream systems relying on this field would incorrectly assume the full sfAmount was delivered. Fixed by the fixMPTDeliveredAmount amendment at lines 619-621.
- **BUG-U006**: Unconditional sandbox apply in IOU payment path regardless of result code In the IOU/ripple payment path, `pv.apply(ctx_.rawView)` at line 520 is called unconditionally after RippleCalc, even if the result is an error. This appears to commit partial state on failure. However, the Transactor::operator framework handles this correctly: for tec errors (the only non-success results that reach the ledger), the context is reset via `reset(fee)` at line 1335, which discards all changes and re-applies only the fee. So partial state from a failed RippleCalc is never committed to the ledger.
- **BUG-G005**: PaymentMint/PaymentBurn granular delegation has no amount cap A delegate with PaymentMint permission can mint unlimited tokens to any destination on behalf of the issuer. A delegate with PaymentBurn permission can burn the entire balance of the delegating account. There is no amount restriction in the granular delegation check. However, this is by design: the issuer explicitly trusts the delegate by creating the delegation entry. The delegation can be revoked at any time via DelegateSet. The lack of amount caps is a deliberate design choice consistent with the broader delegation model where trust is binary (permission granted or not).
- **BUG-G006**: Pre-fixMPTDeliveredAmount: MPT partial payment delivered amount not set in metadata Before the fixMPTDeliveredAmount amendment, when an MPT partial payment delivers less than dstAmount, ctx\_.deliver is not called, meaning the transaction metadata does not contain the correct delivered\_amount. This is a known bug that is fixed by the fixMPTDeliveredAmount amendment. Per the analysis rules, pre-amendment code paths are not bugs.
- **BUG-G007**: Pre-fixSecurity3\_1\_3: Hybrid offers with empty AdditionalBooks pass domain check Before the fixSecurity3\_1\_3 amendment, the offerInDomain function only checked isFieldPresent(sfAdditionalBooks) for hybrid offers but did not check that the array had exactly 1 entry. A hybrid offer with an empty AdditionalBooks array (size 0) would pass the domain check. This is fixed by the fixSecurity3\_1\_3 amendment which requires size == 1.

---

### Additional Context

@Shashwat Mittal @Shawn Xie is this intended behavior?

@Mayukha Vadari it is. If domain is specified in a payment txn that doesn’t interact with DEX, it will simply act as a no-op. But i guess we can also try to restrict it if it’s a non-DEX payment. anyways the current behavior is harmless

@Shawn Xie Agreed it’s harmless, just wanted an answer on whether we’d prefer a no-op or an error.
